page: Microsoft Azure E4ds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the EDSv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. Operating at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz, the x86_64 processor includes a 35 MB L3 cache and supports AVX-512 vector instructions, including AVX512_VNNI for vector neural network operations. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core.

For storage, the E4ds_v4 includes a 154 GB local SSD and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the server exhibits moderate single-core capabilities, with average performance in Geekbench single-core and single-threaded gzip compression. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and large-block memory read/write operations, fall into the lower performance tiers. Database operations and Redis SET benchmarks also register in the bottom quartile, indicating that while memory capacity is high, raw throughput is constrained by the 4-vCPU allocation.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ds_v4 offers a dense memory profile and local SSD storage without the premium cost of larger compute instances, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput. It is well-suited for small-scale databases, caching layers, text processing, and lightweight web serving where memory capacity is prioritized over raw computational speed.
